results: Pending counteroffer closes directly, saves both ledgers, and never fabricates a response or signature.
Reopening and saving the same total does not duplicate a payment or engagement.
A 50 deposit plus a total of 120 adds only 70, keeps real signatures, and retains 30 due.
Reducing a total records an explicit negative adjustment without deleting payment history.
Zero, partial, excess, and decimal payments keep the actual fee and exact balance.
Blank, negative, malformed, and overprecise amounts are blocked visibly.
Invalid dates and missing roles cannot create a settlement.
The direct payment flow cannot rewrite an agreed fee or signed contract.
Rapid repeated taps produce one conditional write and one payment.
Network failure leaves the cloud unchanged and enables a safe retry.
A lost success response is recovered without charging or recording twice.
A payment added after opening the form must be reviewed before closure.
Conditional writes preserve an update made between the final read and save.
A local refresh failure cannot undo cloud success; the next sync restores the ledger.
A second device imports paid history and closure without overwriting cloud payments.
Unlinked local crew can be closed offline, retaining signatures and previous payments.
A failed local save rolls back the payment and closure together.
Normal payout mirroring preserves unseen remote payments and updates a closed balance.
Explicit payment removal deletes only that entry and retains other cloud history.
The finance card exposes the new action and clearly labels admin closure.
Reproduced 6.9 mixed client receipts; 6.10 separates 150 Express from 200 deposit and keeps 800 due.
Finance shows separate client and Express amounts without migrating or altering existing entries.
Express always adds to income after the package is paid, while the client collection stays 1000.
Large Express sales cannot pay a package; cash and expected profit include Express exactly once.
Refusal adds one unpaid 300 surcharge per wedding and preserves the original signed package and Express sales.
Visible partial and full surcharge payments update only client receipts and cannot double-save.
An unpaid refusal charge can be removed and reapplied without accumulating duplicate fees.
A paid surcharge cannot be removed by erasing its payment history.
Invalid amounts and overpayments leave the 300 surcharge unchanged with visible feedback.
A nonexistent payment date is rejected.
Comma decimal amounts are recorded precisely in the client ledger.
Storage failure rolls back both new charges and payments, and supports retry.
The refusal appears in the supplementary service record without rewriting signed terms or signatures.
Screen and printable reports keep client and Express income in separate columns.
Both ledgers use the existing wedding date filter and reject reversed ranges.
Backup retains Express entries, the refusal charge, and the previous admin closure feature.
An open payment form stays attached to its original wedding even if selection changes.
Package discounts do not discount the separate fixed 300 refusal charge.
Reproduced old Android behavior: hidden confirm cancels acceptance.
Visible confirmation and Cancel perform no write.
Double click saves one fee+contract update; cache and finance persist without duplicate crew.
Connection failure shows an error, keeps the offer unchanged, and supports retry.
Failed pre-save read cannot accept an unverified offer.
Changed price is displayed as an error and is not accepted silently.
Database object key ordering cannot block an unchanged price.
Missing, blank, negative, and malformed fees cannot be accepted.
Pending, rejected, and role-free responses stay blocked with visible feedback.
Zero-fee and decimal accepted counteroffers retain their exact price.
Already confirmed contract is preserved without another write.
A later refresh error cannot turn a completed save into a failure.
